jobs.prompt: The test named a remote command failure fails that job only and never the run in tests/executors-run.test.mjs failed once in CI on macOS (and passes elsewhere) at the assertion that at least 2 jobs completed. Cause: it assumes that of 4 jobs at least 2 are placed on the healthy local host, but placement depends on timing: the failing remote host rejects instantly, frees its slot at once and can be handed the next job again, so on a busy runner all or most jobs can land on the failing host. The behavior under test is only that a remote command failure fails exactly the jobs that ran on that host, and never the run or the other jobs. Make the test deterministic without changing what it proves: drop the assertion on a minimum number of completed jobs and instead assert, for every job, using its hostUses (the last host used): a job whose last host is the failing host (dev2) is failed with an error matching host-exit: 2; a job whose last host is local is complete; no job is cancelled; the run status is not a coordinator failure and the error text has no Coordinator failed; and the total of complete plus failed jobs equals 4. Keep the other assertions that already hold. If hostUses can be empty for a job that failed before placement, treat it as failed with the host-exit error. No sleeps, no timing thresholds. Write only tests/executors-run.test.mjs and change only that one test. ALSO: line 13 of tests/executors-run.test.mjs defines const env with OPENAI_API_KEY set to a long placeholder string that the repository secret scan flags as a possible generic secret assignment. Replace only that value with the obviously fake text test-not-a-secret (no key or token shape), and check that no test in the file depends on the old value (search the file for it); do not add any allow-list or scan exception. Make sure the finished file contains no other long random-looking literal.
